entities.name: Cholera
entities.description: Acute, life-threatening diarrhoeal infection caused by toxigenic Vibrio cholerae (serogroups O1 and O139), characterized by sudden explosive onset of profuse, painless secretory rice-water diarrhea, rapid severe dehydration, and fatal hypovolemic shock within hours if untreated.

entities.name: Rice-water diarrhea
entities.description: Copious, watery, non-bilious, grayish-white diarrheal effluent containing suspended flecks of mucus and epithelial cells with a faintly fishy odor.

entities.name: Explosive stool onset
entities.description: Sudden, unexpected onset of hyper-voluminous diarrhea without prodromal abdominal pain, tenesmus, or fever.

entities.name: Massive volume purging
entities.description: Extreme diarrheal fluid loss often exceeding 500-1000 mL/hr, accumulating to 10-20 liters per day in untreated cholera gravis.

entities.name: Dehydration-induced hypovolemia
entities.description: Rapid contraction of the effective intravascular and interstitial volume resulting from massive luminal fluid translocation.

entities.name: Hypovolemic shock
entities.description: Critical circulatory failure with tissue hypoperfusion, severe hypotension, and metabolic collapse occurring within hours of onset.

entities.name: Cholera sicca
entities.description: Rare, lethal presentation where massive fluid transudation pools within paralytic bowel loops causing fatal shock before diarrhea is evacuated.

entities.name: Effortless vomiting
entities.description: Sudden, clear, watery projectile emesis occurring without antecedent nausea or retching shortly after diarrheal onset.

entities.name: Severe muscle cramps
entities.description: Painful tonic skeletal muscle contractions caused by acute loss of potassium, magnesium, and bicarbonate in cholera effluent.

entities.name: Gastrocnemius cramps
entities.description: Agonizing painful contractures localized to the calf muscles driven by rapid electrolyte depletion and tissue hypoperfusion.

entities.name: Abdominal wall cramps
entities.description: Painful paroxysmal contractions of the rectus abdominis musculature mimicking an acute abdomen without true peritoneal signs.

entities.name: Severe thirst
entities.description: Intense, unquenchable polydipsia driven by hyperosmolar dehydration and baroreceptor activation from intravascular collapse.

entities.name: Oliguria
entities.description: Drastic reduction in urine output (<0.5 mL/kg/h) secondary to compensatory renal vasoconstriction and hypoperfusion.

entities.name: Complete anuria
entities.description: Total cessation of renal urine output signaling critical prerenal failure or acute tubular necrosis in severe shock.

entities.name: Prerenal azotemia
entities.description: Functional acute kidney impairment characterized by elevated BUN and creatinine with preserved tubular integrity.

entities.name: Acute tubular necrosis
entities.description: Ischemic renal parenchymal injury resulting from prolonged uncorrected hypovolemic shock and severe renal ischemia.

entities.name: Non-gap metabolic acidosis
entities.description: Systemic acidemia characterized by normal anion gap early on, caused by catastrophic enteric bicarbonate loss (40-50 mEq/L).

entities.name: Profound base deficit
entities.description: Extreme exhaustion of systemic buffering capacity with base excess often falling below -15 to -20 mEq/L.

entities.name: Kussmaul respirations
entities.description: Deep, rapid, labored breathing pattern functioning as a respiratory compensation for severe metabolic acidemia.

entities.name: Severe hypokalemia
entities.description: Total body potassium exhaustion caused by massive fecal potassium wasting of 20 to 30 mEq/L in cholera stool.

entities.name: Hypokalemic paralytic ileus
entities.description: Loss of normal bowel peristalsis and intestinal atony provoked by severe intracellular potassium depletion.

entities.name: Cardiac dysrhythmias
entities.description: Ventricular ectopy, conduction delays, and asystole triggered by combined hypokalemia, hypomagnesemia, and acidemia.

entities.name: Marked lethargy
entities.description: Severe drowsiness and dulling of mental alertness reflecting reduced cerebral blood flow and metabolic exhaustion.

entities.name: Somnolence
entities.description: Pathologic sleepiness where the patient drifts off unless actively stimulated, seen in progressive cholera shock.

entities.name: Coma
entities.description: Complete unresponsiveness in end-stage, unresuscitated cholera gravis preceding cardiovascular collapse.

entities.name: Peripheral cyanosis
entities.description: Dusky bluish discoloration of distal extremities, nail beds, and lips due to intense peripheral vasoconstriction.

entities.name: Hypothermia
entities.description: Subnormal core body temperature (<36.0°C) developing in severe cholera shock due to evaporative heat loss and poor perfusion.

entities.name: Hypoglycemia
entities.description: Critical reduction in blood glucose (<2.2 mmol/L), especially frequent in pediatric cholera due to depleted hepatic glycogen.

entities.name: Hypoglycemic seizures
entities.description: Generalized convulsive episodes occurring primarily in children with severe cholera secondary to neuroglycopenia.

entities.name: Pediatric altered sensorium
entities.description: Acute encephalopathy and unresponsiveness in pediatric cholera caused by hypoglycemia, severe acidosis, and shock.

entities.name: Maternal hypovolemic miscarriage
entities.description: Spontaneous abortion or premature labor occurring in pregnant women with cholera due to uterine and placental hypoperfusion.

entities.name: Fetal demise
entities.description: Intrauterine fetal death in third-trimester cholera caused by maternal hypovolemic shock, acidosis, and placental insufficiency.

entities.name: Severe hemoconcentration
entities.description: Pronounced contraction of intravascular plasma volume causing elevated concentration of cellular and macromolecular elements.

entities.name: Loss of skin turgor
entities.description: Reduction of skin elasticity and dermal recoil due to severe loss of interstitial hydration fluid.

entities.name: Profound asthenia
entities.description: Overwhelming skeletal muscular weakness and prostration leaving the patient unable to stand or sit unassisted.

entities.name: Postural dizziness
entities.description: Lightheadedness, pre-syncope, and blurred vision elicited when attempting to sit or stand due to orthostatic hypotension.

entities.name: Syncope
entities.description: Transient loss of consciousness resulting from acute cerebral hypoperfusion upon upright positioning.

entities.name: Dry oral mucosa
entities.description: Extreme mucosal dryness with parched buccal surfaces and dry cracked lips resulting from total fluid depletion.

entities.name: Absent tear secretion
entities.description: Total cessation of lacrimal gland output during crying or corneal irritation secondary to severe dehydration.

entities.name: Acute body weight loss
entities.description: Rapid loss exceeding 10% of total body weight within several hours, diagnostic of severe dehydration.

entities.name: Peripheral circulatory collapse
entities.description: Terminal hemodynamic decompensation with unmeasurable arterial pressures and diffuse microcirculatory stasis.

entities.name: Rice-water stool hallmark
entities.description: Translucent grayish-white watery stool with suspended mucus flecks, non-bloody, with faint fishy or sweet odor.

entities.name: Washerwoman hands
entities.description: Deeply shriveled, wrinkled, macerated skin of the palmar surfaces and fingertips identical to prolonged water immersion.

entities.name: Hollow sunken orbits
entities.description: Deeply recessed eyeballs with sunken periorbital sulci and visible orbital rim contours resulting from intraocular and retrobulbar fluid loss.

entities.name: Delayed skin pinch
entities.description: Skin fold pinched across the abdominal wall remains tented and retracts very slowly (>2 seconds), diagnostic of severe dehydration.

entities.name: Vox cholerica
entities.description: Characteristic hoarse, husky whisper or aphonia caused by vocal cord dryness, vocal ligament exhaustion, and severe dehydration.

entities.name: Impalpable radial pulse
entities.description: Absence or severe attenuation of the peripheral radial artery pulsation indicating critical systolic hypotension (<80 mmHg).

entities.name: Cold clammy extremities
entities.description: Frigid, diaphoresis-coated, pale hands and feet resulting from intense sympathetic vasoconstriction in hypovolemic shock.

entities.name: Prolonged capillary refill
entities.description: Capillary bed reperfusion delay exceeding 3 to 4 seconds following nailbed compression reflecting severe peripheral hypoperfusion.

entities.name: Scaphoid abdomen
entities.description: Markedly sunken, carinate, concave abdominal contour resulting from visceral volume deflation and loss of intra-abdominal turgor.

entities.name: Painless abdominal palpation
entities.description: Completely soft, non-tender abdominal exam devoid of involuntary guarding, rigidity, or focal rebound tenderness.

entities.name: Sunken anterior fontanelle
entities.description: Deep depression of the unclosed anterior fontanelle below the surrounding calvarium in infants with severe dehydration.

entities.name: Parched tongue
entities.description: Dry, rough, fissured, and leathery dorsal tongue mucosa devoid of saliva and buccal secretions.

entities.name: Tachypnea
entities.description: Rapid respiratory rate (>24-30 breaths/min in adults) reflecting compensatory respiratory alkalosis for metabolic acidosis.

entities.name: Extreme tachycardia
entities.description: Marked elevation of resting heart rate (>120-140 bpm) compensatory for catastrophic stroke volume reduction.

entities.name: Severe arterial hypotension
entities.description: Systolic blood pressure below 80 mmHg or completely unmeasurable by cuff sphygmomanometry.

entities.name: Narrowed pulse pressure
entities.description: Narrowing of systolic-diastolic differential (<20-25 mmHg) reflecting profound stroke volume reduction with severe vasoconstriction.

entities.name: Absent peripheral reflexes
entities.description: Symmetrical absence or marked dampening of deep tendon reflexes (patellar, Achilles) secondary to severe hypokalemia.

entities.name: Carpopedal spasm
entities.description: Involuntary tonic flexion of wrist and metacarpophalangeal joints with foot plantarflexion caused by alkalotic or electrolyte shifts.

entities.name: Stuporous sensorium
entities.description: Depressed level of consciousness where the patient only arouses briefly to painful or vigorous tactile stimuli.

entities.name: Dull lackluster corneas
entities.description: Loss of corneal luster, dull dry corneal surface, and incomplete lid closure due to severe fluid depletion.

entities.name: Absence of tears
entities.description: Complete lack of lacrimation upon crying or conjunctival stimulation, establishing severe pediatric dehydration.

entities.name: Muscle fasciculations
entities.description: Fine, spontaneous, visible twitches of muscle fiber bundles in large exhausted muscle groups caused by electrolyte shifts.

entities.name: Pale ashen facies
entities.description: Marked facial pallor with a leaden, dusky gray tint and hollow temples characteristic of critical shock.

entities.name: Flaccid muscle tone
entities.description: Generalized muscular hypotonia and loss of resistance to passive joint movement caused by extreme hypokalemia.

entities.name: Weak carotid pulse
entities.description: Severe dampening of central carotid artery pulsations signaling impending complete circulatory arrest.

entities.name: Absent axillary sweat
entities.description: Completely dry axillary vaults confirming profound systemic hypovolemia and anhydrosis.

entities.name: Hyperactive bowel sounds
entities.description: High-pitched, continuous, rushing, and tinkling borborygmi on abdominal auscultation reflecting hyperperistalsis.

entities.name: Orthostatic blood pressure drop
entities.description: Postural drop in systolic BP >20 mmHg or diastolic >10 mmHg with reflex tachycardia upon standing.

entities.name: Shooting-star motility
entities.description: Classic scintillating, rapidly darting bacterial motility observed in fresh rice-water stool under darkfield microscopy.

entities.name: Antiserum motility immobilization
entities.description: Instantaneous cessation of darting vibrio motility upon addition of specific polyvalent O1 or O139 antisera.

entities.name: Acellular stool smear
entities.description: Complete microscopic absence of polymorphonuclear leukocytes (pus cells) and red blood cells on methylene blue stain.

entities.name: Elevated hematocrit
entities.description: Marked rise in hematocrit (typically 50% to 65%) reflecting severe acute plasma volume depletion.

entities.name: Markedly elevated hemoglobin
entities.description: Hemoglobin concentration exceeding 18-20 g/dL resulting from extreme intravascular hemoconcentration.

entities.name: Stress neutrophilic leukocytosis
entities.description: Elevated total white blood cell count (15,000-25,000/uL) with neutrophil predominance driven by catecholamine demargination.

entities.name: Normal platelet count
entities.description: Preserved thrombocyte count on admission CBC, ruling out consumption coagulopathy, septic DIC, or viral thrombocytopenia.

entities.name: Collapsed serum bicarbonate
entities.description: Profound drop in serum bicarbonate (<8-12 mEq/L) caused by massive enteric alkaline fluid excretion.

entities.name: Severe arterial acidemia
entities.description: Arterial blood gas pH collapsing below 7.15-7.25 with marked negative base excess.

entities.name: Massive base deficit
entities.description: Base excess worsening to -12 to -20 mEq/L, quantifying the extreme loss of systemic buffer capacity.

entities.name: Severe fecal bicarbonate loss
entities.description: Fecal bicarbonate concentration reaching 40-50 mEq/L, twice the concentration of normal plasma.

entities.name: Massive fecal potassium loss
entities.description: Fecal potassium concentration reaching 20-30 mEq/L, rapidly depleting whole-body potassium stores.

entities.name: Pseudonormal initial potassium
entities.description: Serum potassium appearing falsely normal or slightly elevated initially due to acidemia-induced extracellular proton-potassium exchange.

entities.name: Post-resuscitation hypokalemia
entities.description: Precipitous plunge in serum potassium following bicarbonate resuscitation as potassium shifts back into cells.

entities.name: Elevated blood urea nitrogen
entities.description: Markedly elevated blood urea nitrogen concentration reflecting reduced glomerular filtration and intense tubular reabsorption.

entities.name: Elevated serum creatinine
entities.description: Rapid rise in serum creatinine from severe prerenal hypoperfusion or acute tubular injury.

entities.name: Elevated BUN creatinine ratio
entities.description: BUN-to-creatinine ratio exceeding 20:1, characteristic of prerenal azotemia resulting from hypoperfusion.

entities.name: Elevated urine specific gravity
entities.description: Urine specific gravity >1.030 with low fractional excretion of sodium (<1%) during oliguric compensation.

entities.name: Normal serum sodium
entities.description: Near-normal serum sodium (135-145 mEq/L) reflecting the isotonic nature of cholera stool fluid losses.

entities.name: Mild serum hyponatremia
entities.description: Modest serum sodium reduction (128-134 mEq/L) seen in patients who ingested large volumes of solute-free water prior to triage.

entities.name: Hyperlactatemia
entities.description: Elevated serum lactate concentration (>4-8 mmol/L) reflecting widespread tissue hypoperfusion and anaerobic metabolism.

entities.name: Elevated serum total protein
entities.description: Elevation of total serum protein (>8.5-10.0 g/dL) driven by intravascular water loss concentrating circulating macromolecules.

entities.name: Elevated serum albumin
entities.description: Hyperalbuminemia (>5.0-6.0 g/dL) resulting purely from acute hemoconcentration.

entities.name: Stool darkfield microscopy
entities.description: Rapid point-of-care wet mount test directly visualizing darting vibrios in cholera diarrhea.

entities.name: Cholera dipstick antigen test
entities.description: Rapid immunochromatographic point-of-care dipstick detecting Vibrio cholerae O1 and O139 lipopolysaccharide within 15 minutes.

entities.name: TCBS yellow colonies
entities.description: Growth of characteristic large, smooth, yellow sucrose-fermenting colonies on Thiosulfate Citrate Bile Salts Sucrose agar.

entities.name: Positive oxidase test
entities.description: Instant deep purple color reaction upon applying oxidase reagent to bacterial colonies, differentiating vibrios from enterobacteria.

entities.name: Gram-negative comma bacillus
entities.description: Microscopic Gram stain finding demonstrating small, curved, comma-shaped Gram-negative rods.

entities.name: Stool PCR amplification
entities.description: Molecular polymerase chain reaction detecting specific ctxA and tcpA genes encoding cholera toxin and toxin coregulated pilus.

entities.name: Positive string test
entities.description: Formation of a persistent mucoid string lifted with an inoculation loop when bacterial colonies are mixed with 0.5% sodium deoxycholate.

entities.name: Vibriocidal antibody titer rise
entities.description: Four-fold or greater rise in serum vibriocidal antibody titer between acute and convalescent phase sera.

entities.name: Flat inferior vena cava
entities.description: Completely slit-like, flat, or non-visualized IVC with >50% inspiratory collapsibility on bedside ultrasound.

entities.name: Hyperdynamic left ventricle
entities.description: Cardiac ultrasound demonstrating an underfilled, kissing-wall hyperdynamic left ventricle in hypovolemic shock.

entities.name: Distended fluid-filled bowel
entities.description: Bedside abdominal ultrasound demonstrating dilated, fluid-filled, hyperactive small bowel loops without mural thickening.

entities.name: Preserved bowel wall thickness
entities.description: Normal small intestinal mural thickness (<2-3 mm) on ultrasound, ruling out transmural inflammation or ischemic bowel.

entities.name: Absent peritoneal fluid
entities.description: Bedside focused abdominal sonography (FAST) demonstrating dry dependent recesses, ruling out hemoperitoneum or inflammatory ascites.

entities.name: Peaked P waves
entities.description: Electrocardiographic finding of tall, peaked P waves (>2.5 mm in lead II) caused by severe hypokalemia and right atrial strain.

entities.name: Flattened T waves
entities.description: Electrocardiographic flattening or inversion of T waves and emergence of prominent U waves caused by severe hypokalemia.

entities.name: Contaminated drinking water
entities.description: Ingestion of municipal, well, or surface water contaminated with human fecal material containing Vibrio cholerae.

entities.name: Inadequate WASH infrastructure
entities.description: Collapse or lack of clean water, basic sanitation, and hygiene infrastructure in resource-limited or disaster settings.

entities.name: Raw contaminated shellfish
entities.description: Ingestion of raw or undercooked bivalves, crabs, and oysters harvested from warm estuarine waters.

entities.name: Copepod aquatic reservoirs
entities.description: Estuarine zooplankton and copepods whose chitinous surfaces support dense Vibrio cholerae biofilms.

entities.name: Cholera corpse handling
entities.description: Traditional preparation, communal washing, and burial rituals involving bodies of individuals deceased from cholera.

entities.name: Displaced refugee encampments
entities.description: Overcrowded emergency settlements with compromised sanitation and shared latrines following conflict or disasters.

entities.name: Extreme flooding events
entities.description: Monsoons, cyclones, and heavy rains that overwhelm drainage networks and contaminate drinking water reservoirs.

entities.name: Street vendor food
entities.description: Cooked food or cut fruit held at warm ambient temperatures and prepared with contaminated water or unwashed hands.

entities.name: Asymptomatic household contacts
entities.description: Close contacts of infected individuals who shed viable vibrios in feces for up to 14 days without developing severe illness.

entities.name: Estuarine water contact
entities.description: Occupational or recreational exposure to warm, brackish estuarine and coastal waters harboring endemic vibrios.

entities.name: Blood group O
entities.description: Inherited ABO blood group O phenotype predisposing individuals to severe cholera gravis and catastrophic dehydration.

entities.name: Gastric achlorhydria
entities.description: Absence of gastric hydrochloric acid secretion eliminating the normal protective acid barrier against vibrios.

entities.name: Proton pump inhibitor therapy
entities.description: Pharmacologic acid suppression with PPIs or H2 blockers allowing survival of ingested vibrios through the stomach.

entities.name: Severe acute malnutrition
entities.description: Wasting and micronutrient depletion in children causing impaired mucosal defense and heightened dehydration fatality.

entities.name: Advanced HIV infection
entities.description: Immunodeficiency state with low CD4 counts resulting in impaired mucosal immune response and prolonged shedding.

entities.name: Third-trimester pregnancy
entities.description: Late gestational state characterized by physiological volume dependence and high risk of maternal-fetal mortality in shock.

entities.name: Environmental enteropathy
entities.description: Chronic inflammatory small bowel mucosal blunting and barrier dysfunction prevalent in impoverished sanitary conditions.

entities.name: Small bowel bacterial overgrowth
entities.description: Colonization of the upper small intestine by colonic fecal bacteria that modulates mucosal immunology and vaccine responsiveness.

entities.name: Intestinal helminth infection
entities.description: Heavy infection with soil-transmitted nematodes (Ascaris lumbricoides) inducing immune skewing and impaired mucosal response.

entities.name: Hyperacute incubation period
entities.description: Extremely rapid onset of symptoms within 2 to 24 hours following ingestion of a massive bacterial inoculum.

entities.name: Standard incubation period
entities.description: Typical incubation window of 1 to 5 days (median 18 to 48 hours) from pathogen ingestion to onset of watery diarrhea.

entities.name: Vibrio shedding period
entities.description: Convalescent fecal shedding of viable Vibrio cholerae organisms persisting for 1 to 14 days after symptom resolution.

entities.name: High continuous fever
entities.description: Body temperature exceeding 39°C continuously, characteristic of invasive systemic or intracellular pathogens.

entities.name: Macroscopic bloody stool
entities.description: Gross visible red blood, hematochezia, or clots in the diarrheal stool indicating mucosal ulceration.

entities.name: Fecal polymorphonuclear leukocytes
entities.description: Abundant pus cells or sheets of neutrophils on microscopic examination of a stool smear.

entities.name: Stool erythrocytes
entities.description: Microscopic red blood cells in the fecal smear reflecting structural mucosal damage and hemorrhage.

entities.name: Painful rectal tenesmus
entities.description: Severe, painful, ineffective straining at stool pathognomonic of acute rectosigmoid mucosal inflammation.

entities.name: Severe colicky abdominal pain
entities.description: Intensely painful cramping abdominal paroxysms reflecting colonic wall inflammation or peritonitis.

entities.name: Chronic diarrheal duration
entities.description: Diarrheal illness lasting more than 7 to 14 days, indicative of chronic infection or non-infectious malabsorption.

entities.name: Prominent antecedent nausea
entities.description: Protracted nausea and retching preceding diarrheal onset by hours or days, characteristic of viral gastroenteritis.

entities.name: Low volume diarrhea
entities.description: Scant or small-volume stool evacuations (<200-300 mL/day), typical of distal colonic inflammation.

entities.name: Rebound abdominal tenderness
entities.description: Peritoneal signs with sharp tenderness on sudden release of abdominal palpation indicating transmural peritonitis.

entities.name: Bloody vomiting
entities.description: Macroscopic hematemesis or coffee-ground emesis indicating upper gastrointestinal mucosal bleeding.

entities.name: Bilious emesis
entities.description: Dark green or golden-yellow bilious vomiting indicating distal duodenal or mechanical intestinal obstruction.

entities.name: Purulent stool exudate
entities.description: Macroscopic thick mucoid pus in the stool reflecting severe suppurative mucosal inflammation.

entities.name: Rose spots exanthem
entities.description: Salmon-pink blanching macules on the trunk and abdomen pathognomonic of Salmonella Typhi bacteremia.

entities.name: Hepatosplenomegaly
entities.description: Palpable enlargement of the liver and spleen indicating systemic reticuloendothelial infection.

entities.name: Prominent lymphadenopathy
entities.description: Significant enlargement of peripheral or mesenteric lymph node chains reflecting systemic or granulomatous infection.

entities.name: Toxic megacolon
entities.description: Severe, life-threatening colonic distension (>6 cm) with systemic toxicity resulting from transmural colonic inflammation.

entities.name: Pseudomembranes on colonoscopy
entities.description: Raised, yellow-white inflammatory mucosal plaques characteristic of Clostridioides difficile colitis.

entities.name: Intestinal mucosal ulceration
entities.description: Direct endoscopic or histopathologic demonstration of epithelial ulceration and transmural necrosis.

entities.name: Macroscopic fecal odor
entities.description: Overpowering foul or putrid fecal stench typical of invasive or colonic bacterial infections.

entities.name: Melena
entities.description: Black, tarry, foul-smelling stool resulting from upper gastrointestinal bleeding and blood degradation.

entities.name: Marked peripheral eosinophilia
entities.description: Elevated absolute eosinophil count (>1,000/uL) reflecting tissue-invasive helminthic or allergic pathology.

entities.name: Shigella dysenteriae
entities.description: Invasive colonic bacterial pathogen causing bacillary dysentery with high fever, mucosal ulceration, and tenesmus.

entities.name: Campylobacter jejuni enteritis
entities.description: Bacterial pathogen causing acute inflammatory enterocolitis with pseudoappendiceal abdominal pain and bloody diarrhea.

entities.name: Enterotoxigenic Escherichia coli
entities.description: Common cause of traveler's watery diarrhea mediated by LT/ST enterotoxins, typically producing self-limited loose stools.

entities.name: Entamoeba histolytica colitis
entities.description: Invasive colonic protozoan parasite producing gradual dysentery, flask-shaped ulcers, and localized tenderness.

entities.name: Rotavirus gastroenteritis
entities.description: Leading viral cause of severe diarrheal illness in young children, featuring fever, vomiting, and moderate watery stool.

entities.name: Norovirus gastroenteritis
entities.description: Highly contagious viral pathogen causing acute epidemic gastroenteritis dominated by violent projectile vomiting.

entities.name: Salmonella enterica gastroenteritis
entities.description: Non-typhoidal Salmonella causing inflammatory foodborne enteritis with nausea, fever, abdominal cramps, and loose stools.

entities.name: Clostridioides difficile colitis
entities.description: Toxin-mediated colonic disease following antibiotic therapy, causing watery diarrhea, abdominal pain, fever, and leukocytosis.

entities.name: Vibrio parahaemolyticus enteritis
entities.description: Halophilic marine vibrio causing foodborne inflammatory gastroenteritis with severe colic and explosive diarrhea.

entities.name: Giardia duodenalis enteritis
entities.description: Flagellated protozoan causing subacute malabsorptive diarrhea with steatorrhea, foul sulfurous belching, and bloating.

entities.name: Cryptosporidium parvum enteritis
entities.description: Apicomplexan protozoan causing protracted watery diarrhea in immunocompromised hosts and self-limited outbreaks in children.

entities.name: Staphylococcal food poisoning
entities.description: Intoxication caused by ingestion of preformed heat-stable enterotoxin in contaminated food, causing hyperacute violent emesis.

entities.name: Bacillus cereus illness
entities.description: Foodborne illness causing either rapid emetic toxin syndrome or slower diarrheal enterotoxin syndrome with mild cramps.

entities.name: Enteroinvasive Escherichia coli
entities.description: Shigella-like invasive E. coli that invades and destroys the colonic mucosa to cause inflammatory dysentery.

entities.name: Vibrio vulnificus sepsis
entities.description: Invasive marine vibrio infection causing primary septic shock and hemorrhagic bullae in patients with liver disease.

entities.name: VIPoma syndrome
entities.description: Rare neuroendocrine tumor secreting vasoactive intestinal peptide causing chronic unremitting secretory watery diarrhea.

entities.name: Intestinal microsporidiosis
entities.description: Opportunistic microsporidian infection causing chronic watery diarrhea, malabsorption, and wasting in advanced HIV.

entities.name: Salmonella Typhi bacteremia
entities.description: Systemic intracellular bacterial infection presenting with step-ladder fever, relative bradycardia, rose spots, and abdominal pain.

relationships.keywords: HIGH_RISK_HOST, small bowel bacterial overgrowth, SBBO, upper gut colonization, microbiome barrier
relationships.description: [HIGH_RISK_HOST] Small bowel bacterial overgrowth in poverty-associated environments alters luminal bile acids and modulates mucosal susceptibility to enteric pathogens.

relationships.keywords: HIGH_RISK_HOST, intestinal helminths, Ascaris lumbricoides, Th2 skewing, dampened mucosal immunity
relationships.description: [HIGH_RISK_HOST] Heavy chronic intestinal helminthiasis skews mucosal immune responses and impairs protective vibriocidal antibody generation against cholera.

relationships.keywords: INCUBATION_PERIOD, hyperacute incubation, rapid onset hours, short latency, high inoculum
relationships.description: [INCUBATION_PERIOD] Following ingestion of a heavy vibrio inoculum, the incubation period can be hyperacute, with severe diarrhea developing within 2 to 24 hours.

relationships.keywords: INCUBATION_PERIOD, standard incubation, 1 to 5 days, typical latency, epidemic incubation
relationships.description: [INCUBATION_PERIOD] In standard exposure settings, symptoms typically emerge 1 to 5 days following consumption of contaminated food or water.

relationships.keywords: INCUBATION_PERIOD, vibrio shedding period, fecal shedding duration, convalescent carriage, 14 days
relationships.description: [INCUBATION_PERIOD] Convalescent individuals shed viable Vibrio cholerae in feces for 1 to 14 days, maintaining environmental contamination during outbreaks.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, high fever, continuous pyrexia, invasive sign, cholera exclusion
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] High continuous fever (>39°C) at admission rules out uncomplicated cholera in favor of invasive enteric pathogens like Shigella or Salmonella.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, macroscopic blood, gross hematochezia, dysentery sign, bloody stool exclusion
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Presence of macroscopic red blood or clots in diarrheal effluent rules out classic cholera, indicating an invasive mucosal colitis.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, fecal leukocytes, stool pus cells, sheets of PMNs, inflammatory smear
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Demonstration of abundant fecal polymorphonuclear neutrophils (pus cells) on stool microscopy rules out enterotoxin-driven non-invasive cholera.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, stool erythrocytes, fecal RBCs, microscopic blood, mucosal breach exclusion
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Microscopic identification of erythrocytes on stool wet mount rules out cholera, pointing to invasive mucosal ulceration.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, painful tenesmus, rectal straining, rectosigmoid spasm, dysentery hallmark
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Painful rectal tenesmus and colonic straining rule out cholera, which presents with effortless and painless fluid evacuation.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, colicky abdominal pain, severe cramps, painful colic, inflammatory diarrhea
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Severe colicky abdominal pain and peritoneal cramps rule out uncomplicated cholera, where diarrhea is characteristically effortless and painless.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, chronic diarrhea, prolonged duration, persistent diarrhea, timeline exclusion
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Diarrheal persistence exceeding 7 to 14 days rules out acute cholera, which presents hyperacutely and runs a course of 2 to 6 days.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, antecedent nausea, protracted retching, pre-diarrheal nausea, viral pattern
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Protracted antecedent nausea and dry heaving prior to diarrhea onset rules out cholera, where effortless vomiting follows diarrhea.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, low volume diarrhea, scant stools, small volume evacuations, non-cholera volume
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Low-volume stool output (<300 mL/day) rules out cholera, which is defined by astronomical fluid losses of 500-1000 mL/hour.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, rebound tenderness, peritonitis signs, abdominal guarding, acute surgical abdomen
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Presence of abdominal rebound tenderness or involuntary guarding rules out cholera, indicating acute peritonitis or bowel perforation.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, bloody vomiting, hematemesis, coffee ground emesis, mucosal bleeding
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Hematemesis or coffee-ground vomiting rules out the clear non-bilious watery emesis characteristic of acute cholera.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, bilious emesis, green vomiting, bile-stained vomit, mechanical obstruction
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Copious bilious green vomiting rules out cholera's clear gastric transudate, indicating mechanical small bowel obstruction.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, purulent stool exudate, mucopus, frank pus, suppurative colitis
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Presence of thick macroscopic pus in the stool rules out cholera's translucent rice-water effluent in favor of severe dysentery.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, rose spots, salmon macules, trunk rash, typhoid exanthem
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Presence of erythematous rose spots on the trunk rules out cholera, indicating systemic Salmonella Typhi or Paratyphi infection.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, hepatosplenomegaly, organomegaly, palpable spleen, systemic infection
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Palpable hepatosplenomegaly rules out purely luminal cholera infection, pointing toward visceral leishmaniasis, malaria, or typhoid fever.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, lymphadenopathy, enlarged lymph nodes, mesenteric adenitis, systemic pathogen
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Prominent peripheral or mesenteric lymphadenopathy rules out cholera, which does not produce localized or generalized lymph node enlargement.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, toxic megacolon, colonic dilatation, transmural colitis, fulminant colitis
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Massive acute dilatation of the colon on imaging rules out cholera, indicating severe inflammatory or pseudomembranous colitis.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, pseudomembranes, endoscopic plaques, C difficile lesions, pseudomembranous colitis
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Endoscopic visualization of discrete yellow pseudomembranous colonic plaques rules out cholera, confirming Clostridioides difficile.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, mucosal ulceration, mucosal cratering, epithelial necrosis, invasive enteropathy
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Demonstration of mucosal ulcerations or architectural friability on endoscopy rules out non-invasive cholera enteropathy.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, foul fecal odor, putrid smell, offensive stool, colonic stench
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Overpowering foul, putrid fecal odor rules out the characteristic inoffensive, faintly fishy or sweet odor of cholera rice-water stool.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, melena, black tarry stool, upper GI bleed, digested blood
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Melenic tarry stool rules out cholera, indicating significant digested blood from upper gastrointestinal bleeding.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, marked eosinophilia, high eosinophil count, parasitic allergy, tissue invasion
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Marked peripheral blood eosinophilia rules out acute bacterial cholera in favor of invasive helminthic or eosinophilic gastroenteritis.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, Shigella dysenteriae, bacillary dysentery, bloody diarrhea, tenesmus contrast
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Shigella dysenteriae presents with high fever (>39°C), severe colicky cramps, tenesmus, and scant bloody-mucoid stools with abundant leukocytes; cholera presents with afebrile, painless, multi-liter non-bloody rice-water diarrhea and an acellular stool smear.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, Campylobacter jejuni, pseudoappendicitis, inflammatory enteritis, bloody stool contrast
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Campylobacter jejuni presents with prominent periumbilical or right-lower-quadrant pain, fever, and inflammatory bloody diarrhea; cholera produces painless, massive non-bloody rice-water purging without peritoneal signs or fever.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, ETEC, traveler's diarrhea, self-limited diarrhea, low volume contrast
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] ETEC produces mild to moderate watery diarrhea (3-5 stools/day, rarely >1-2 L/day) resolving within 3-5 days; cholera gravis causes catastrophic purging (10-20 L/day, >500-1000 mL/hr) leading to hypovolemic shock within hours.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, Entamoeba histolytica, amoebic dysentery, subacute colitis, trophozoite contrast
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Entamoeba histolytica has an insidious onset over 1-3 weeks with localized right-lower-quadrant tenderness and bloody-mucoid stools containing hematophagous trophozoites; cholera has an explosive hyperacute onset with painless rice-water diarrhea.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, Rotavirus gastroenteritis, pediatric rotavirus, viral diarrhea, antecedent vomiting contrast
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Rotavirus presents in young infants with high fever and protracted vomiting preceding diarrhea by 24-48 hours with moderate purge volume; cholera strikes all age groups with abrupt effortless diarrhea followed by emesis, lack of fever, and astronomical purging volumes.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, Norovirus gastroenteritis, winter vomiting disease, projectile vomiting, epidemic gastroenteritis contrast
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Norovirus causes acute explosive projectile vomiting as the dominant symptom alongside mild-to-moderate diarrhea resolving in 24-48 hours; cholera presents primarily with massive lower-tract fluid purging exceeding 10-20 L/day without preceding nausea.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, Salmonella enterica, non-typhoidal salmonellosis, foodborne enteritis, foul stool contrast
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Non-typhoidal Salmonella presents with fever, nausea, painful periumbilical cramping, and foul-smelling greenish loose stools containing fecal leukocytes; cholera is characterized by painless, afebrile, non-inflammatory rice-water effluent.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, Clostridioides difficile, pseudomembranous colitis, antibiotic diarrhea, leukocytosis contrast
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Clostridioides difficile colitis typically follows antimicrobial exposure and features painful diarrhea, fever, marked leukocytosis, and endoscopic pseudomembranes; cholera arises from contaminated water/food and produces painless acellular rice-water purging.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, Vibrio parahaemolyticus, seafood food poisoning, inflammatory vibrio, colic contrast
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Vibrio parahaemolyticus causes acute inflammatory gastroenteritis with severe colicky abdominal cramps, vomiting, fever, and occasionally bloody stool following seafood ingestion; cholera causes afebrile, completely painless rice-water purging driven by cholera toxin.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, Giardia duodenalis, giardiasis, steatorrhea, chronic malabsorption contrast
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Giardiasis produces subacute or chronic greasy, foul-smelling, malodorous stools with abdominal bloating, flatulence, and weight loss over weeks; cholera is a hyperacute secretory process with non-malodorous watery effluent lasting days.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, Cryptosporidium parvum, cryptosporidiosis, chronic diarrhea, opportunistic parasite contrast
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Cryptosporidiosis presents with chronic or protracted watery diarrhea lasting weeks in immunocompromised hosts with modified acid-fast oocysts in stool; cholera causes hyperacute, self-limiting (if resuscitated) multi-liter secretory purging over 2 to 6 days.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, Staphylococcal food poisoning, preformed enterotoxin, rapid emesis, food intoxication contrast
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Staphylococcal food poisoning presents abruptly with violent emesis and retching within 1-6 hours of food ingestion and resolves in 24 hours; cholera is an active intestinal infection presenting predominantly with massive multi-liter watery diarrhea.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, Bacillus cereus, fried rice syndrome, diarrheal toxin, emetic toxin contrast
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Bacillus cereus diarrheal syndrome causes mild-to-moderate watery diarrhea with colicky cramps resolving within 24 hours without shock; cholera causes life-threatening multi-liter purging leading to fatal hypovolemic shock within hours.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, EIEC, enteroinvasive E coli, inflammatory dysentery, mucosal invasion contrast
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] EIEC invades the colonic epithelium causing fever, severe lower abdominal cramping, tenesmus, and purulent bloody stool; cholera causes enterotoxin-mediated secretion without tissue invasion, mucosal ulceration, or fever.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, Vibrio vulnificus, marine bacteremia, hemorrhagic bullae, septic shock contrast
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Vibrio vulnificus causes fulminant bacteremia with hemorrhagic bullous skin lesions, necrotizing fasciitis, and septic shock in cirrhotic hosts; Vibrio cholerae remains confined to the gut lumen, causing severe secretory diarrhea and hypovolemic shock.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, VIPoma syndrome, Verner-Morrison syndrome, pancreatic cholera, chronic diarrhea contrast
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] VIPoma (Verner-Morrison syndrome) causes chronic, persistent secretory watery diarrhea lasting months with achlorhydria and hypokalemia; cholera presents with hyperacute epidemic watery diarrhea resolving within days upon clearance.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, Intestinal microsporidiosis, microsporidia, opportunistic AIDS diarrhea, chronic wasting contrast
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Microsporidiosis causes chronic debilitating watery diarrhea and wasting over months in patients with severe CD4 lymphopenia; cholera causes explosive, acute, self-terminating multi-liter purging in both healthy and immunocompromised hosts.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, Salmonella Typhi, typhoid fever, enteric fever, step-ladder fever contrast
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Salmonella Typhi presents with insidious step-ladder fever, headache, relative bradycardia, rose spots, and constipation or pea-soup diarrhea with bacteremia; cholera presents with afebrile, explosive, hyper-voluminous rice-water diarrhea without bacteremia.
